final_answer:
Yes. In this donor-level PBMC composition analysis, SLE-associated immune-cell changes differed between Asian and European-ancestry participants.

Using per-donor cell-type proportions from 261 Asian/European donors (Asian SLE n=83, Asian controls n=24, European SLE n=75, European controls n=74), four of 11 cell types showed significant disease-by-ancestry interactions after FDR correction. The strongest difference was CD4-positive T cells: Asian donors showed a much larger SLE-associated decrease (mean 42.17% in controls to 21.94% in SLE) than European donors (35.96% to 28.28%; interaction diff-in-diff -12.55 percentage points, q=2.0e-05). Plasmacytoid dendritic cells showed stronger depletion in European SLE than Asian SLE (q=1.73e-04). B cells and CD8-positive T cells showed relative increases in Asian SLE compared with European SLE patterns (B-cell interaction q=0.035; CD8 T-cell interaction q=0.0365).

Thus, the shared SLE signature included increased monocyte proportions and reduced CD4 T-cell proportions, but the magnitude and lineage pattern differed by ancestry: Asian SLE was characterized by stronger CD4 T-cell loss and relatively higher CD8/B-cell proportions, whereas European SLE showed stronger circulating pDC and dendritic/B-cell depletion. These are observational cell-proportion associations, not causal treatment-response evidence, and should be validated with absolute counts, treatment/severity covariates, and longitudinal or response data.
